historyTimeline.h2: Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.0 TFSI was introduced to the Q5 range, it provided a potent, turbocharged petrol alternative to the dominant TDI diesels. Over its production run, it evolved from the EA888 Gen 2 to the highly refined Gen 3 and Gen 3b units, adopting mild-hybrid technology and the modern "40/45 TFSI" badging convention.

milestones.description: CAEB engine code introduced (211hp), establishing the 2.0 TFSI in the 8R generation.
CDNB engine code introduced (211hp), featuring updated EA888 Gen 3 components to reduce oil consumption and improve reliability.
CYRB engine code introduced (252hp) for the FY generation, badged as 45 TFSI, with revised turbocharging and dual-injection systems.
DKZA / DKNB engine codes introduced (245hp/265hp) for the FY facelift, integrating 12V mild-hybrid (MHEV) systems for improved efficiency and emissions compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI is generally robust, particularly in its Gen 3 and Gen 3b iterations. However, specific components carry known vulnerabilities. The CAEB and CDNB codes dominate earlier replacement demand for this variant due to timing chain and cooling system weaknesses. Rebuilt engines sourced through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Water Pump & Thermostat Housing Failure - Why the Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI (CDNB, CYRB, DKZA, 2012-present)
problems.rootCause: Plastic components within the integrated water pump and thermostat housing warp and crack under sustained heat cycles, leading to gradual coolant loss and potential overheating if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of water pump and thermostat housing assembly
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as preventative maintenance at 80k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded cooling components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if coolant loss has caused catastrophic overheating and cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: For the 2.0 TFSI, preventative replacement of the water pump and thermostat housing is highly advised before catastrophic failure occurs. If you are dealing with an earlier CAEB unit that has suffered timing chain failure, a rebuilt engine with the revised Gen 3 components is the most reliable long-term solution.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI (CAEB) Risks Catastrophic Failure
problems.affectedModels: Audi Q5 2.0 TFSI / 40/45 TFSI (CAEB, early CDNB, 2008-2014)
problems.rootCause: Early EA888 Gen 2 tensioners can lose pressure, allowing the timing chain to stretch and potentially skip a tooth, causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Timing chain, guides, and revised tensioner replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early via cold-start rattle diagnosis before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt unit with Gen 3 revised timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain skip has caused secondary valve or piston damage
